statement_modern: For a smooth projective curve C of genus g and divisor D of degree d, dim|D|=h^0(O_C(D))−1≥d−g.

statement_modern: The canonical linear system of a smooth curve is a birational invariant.
repair_and_reference: Enriques–Chisini, Libro V, vol. III; canonical sheaf on the smooth model.

statement_modern: For a nodal plane model of degree m with normalization of genus g, adjoints of degree m−3+s cut the complete series |K_C+sH|, whenever interpreted with the fixed conductor contributions removed.
repair_and_reference: Plane adjunction/conductor theorem; Enriques–Chisini as cited.
notes: §1; TeX line 15; all integral s, possibly an empty series.

statement_modern: For s sufficiently large, the nodes impose independent conditions on plane forms of degree m−3+s, and |K_C+sH| has degree 2g−2+sm and dimension g−2+sm.

notes: §1; TeX lines 15–23; source writes degree n and dimension n−p.

statement_modern: The number d of ordinary nodes of a plane curve of degree m and geometric genus g equals (m−1)(m−2)/2−g.
repair_and_reference: Normalization exact sequence: each node has delta invariant 1.

statement_modern: After imposing an independent group G on a complete nonspecial linear series of degree n, the residual series has dimension (n−deg G)−g.
repair_and_reference: Subtract the independent linear conditions.

statement_modern: Adjoints of plane degree m−3 cut the complete canonical series of degree 2g−2 and projective dimension g−1; the nodes impose independent conditions at this degree.
repair_and_reference: Canonical adjunction and h^0(K_C)=g.

statement_modern: The index of speciality of a divisor D on a smooth curve is i(D)=h^0(K_C−D)=h^1(O_C(D)).
repair_and_reference: Serre duality.
notes: §1; TeX line 33; vector dimension, not projective dimension.

statement_modern: Curve Riemann–Roch is dim|D|=deg D−g+i(D).
repair_and_reference: Enriques–Chisini, Libro V, vol. III; modern curve Riemann–Roch.

statement_modern: The asymptotic number of conditions imposed by a spatial curve on containing surfaces is given by the Cayley–Noether postulation formulas.
repair_and_reference: Cayley (1870) and Noether (1871), as attributed here; no titles supplied at this point.
notes: §1; TeX line 39; precise cases proved in §2.

statement_modern: For C⊂P^3 and degree n, postulation means the rank of H^0(P^3,O(n))→H^0(C,O_C(n)), hence one plus the dimension of the induced projective series.
repair_and_reference: Restriction exact sequence.

statement_modern: If this induced series is complete and nonspecial on a smooth degree-m genus-g curve, its dimension is mn−g and its postulation is mn−g+1.
repair_and_reference: Curve Riemann–Roch.

statement_modern: Speciality contributes +h^1(O_C(n)) to the expected rank, while incompleteness subtracts the cokernel dimension of the restriction map.

repair_and_reference: Serre duality: K_C−nH has negative degree.

statement_modern: For a smooth nondegenerate spatial curve of degree m and genus g, restriction of degree-n forms is complete and nonspecial for n≥m−2.

statement_modern: A generic projection of such a smooth curve to P^2 is birational with d=(m−1)(m−2)/2−g ordinary nodes; each node lifts to two points of C.

statement_modern: Cones over plane adjoints give a complete nonspecial residual series after removing the 2d preimages G of projection nodes, of degree mn−2d and dimension mn−2d−g.

statement_modern: For n≥m−2 the exact postulation is mn−g+1.

statement_modern: An ordinary noncoplanar triple point of a curve forces a containing surface to have multiplicity at least two there; assigning such a double point imposes four jet conditions.

statement_modern: For large s, the canonical restriction defect of L_s=sH equals p_g−p_a.

statement_modern: Every irreducible moving system satisfies δ(C)≤p_g−p_a.

statement_modern: A surface is regular when p_a=p_g, and otherwise irregular with irregularity q=p_g−p_a.

repair_and_reference: Modern excess is h^1(O_X(D)) when h^2(O_X(D))=0; full convention is refined later.

statement_modern: The preceding multiple-curve postulation formula requires correction when C has singular points.

statement_modern: An assigned s-fold point in P³ imposes binom(s+2,3) linear jet conditions on forms of sufficiently large degree.

statement_modern: Sextic surfaces form P⁸³, and one assigned ordinary triple point imposes ten linear jet conditions.

statement_modern: The system of sextics with this octad of triple points has dimension at most nine.
gap_or_error: Footnote only says to bound it by restricting to a quadric; the bound is not calculated.

repair_and_reference: For X∈|3L| in Bl₈P³, K_X=L|_X; f_*O_X=O_B for a plane cubic B.

notes: §7; TeX lines 680–683; full independent modern derivation in commentary.

statement_modern: For these surfaces p_a=n−1.
repair_and_reference: Relative duality gives R¹f_*O_X=O_B(−1), hence χ(O_X)=n.

statement_modern: The genus of that irrational pencil equals q=p_g−p_a.

notes: §7; TeX line 693; assumes a transverse reduced Cayley octad and general defining polynomial.
